# owid-grapher-py

> A Python library for creating interactive Our World in Data charts in Jupyter
> notebooks. A thin proxy over the `@ourworldindata/grapher` npm package: it
> shapes a pandas DataFrame into the CSV Grapher reads, and passes Grapher's own
> chart config through untouched.

Charts are drawn in the browser by Grapher's standalone bundle, which the
generated HTML loads from OWID's package host. That host is only reachable from
OWID's Tailnet until the npm package is published publicly; set
`OWID_GRAPHER_BUNDLE_URL` to serve the bundle from somewhere else.

## Installation

```bash
pip install owid-grapher-py

# optional, for PNG/SVG export
pip install playwright && playwright install chromium
```

## The whole API

```python
from owid.grapher import Chart

Chart(
    df,                   # a pandas DataFrame
    config={...},         # Grapher's chart config, passed through untouched
    columns={...},        # Grapher's column metadata, keyed by column name
    entity="country",     # which column holds entities (default: found by name)
    time="year",          # which column holds time (default: found by name)
    height=600,           # how tall the chart is in a notebook, in pixels
)
```

`Chart` displays itself in a notebook. `to_html()` returns a standalone page,
`save_png(path)` / `save_svg(path)` render images (via Playwright), and
`export()` returns the CSV, column defs and config handed to Grapher.

There is no other API: no chart-type methods, no encoding calls, no label or
axis helpers. Anything you want to change is a key in `config` or `columns`.

### What the Python side does

- renames the entity column to `entityName` (found by name among `entityName`,
  `entity`, `country`, `location`, or named with `entity=`)
- names the time column `year` for numbers or `date` for dates (found among
  `year`, `date`, `day`, or named with `time=`)
- makes column names slug-safe
- defaults `selectedEntityNames` to the frame's entities, without which line and
  bar charts draw nothing
- rejects config keys Grapher doesn't have, with a did-you-mean suggestion

### What Grapher does, so you don't have to

- derives `ySlugs` from the numeric columns when it isn't given
- opens on the first entry of `chartTypes`
- reads a `date` column of ISO dates as a date timeline
- renders maps and scatter plots without any entity selection

## config: Grapher's chart config

`config` is typed as `GrapherConfig` in `owid.grapher.config`, generated from
Grapher's published JSON schema
(`https://files.ourworldindata.org/schemas/grapher-schema.011.json`), so type
checkers know every key, its type and its enum values. The same keys are what
every chart on ourworldindata.org stores — append `.config.json` to a chart URL
to read one.

Commonly used keys:

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `title`, `subtitle`, `note`, `sourceDesc` | the chart's text |
| `chartTypes` | `["LineChart"]`, `["DiscreteBar"]`, `["StackedDiscreteBar"]`, `["StackedArea"]`, `["StackedBar"]`, `["ScatterPlot"]`, `["SlopeChart"]`, `["Marimekko"]`, `["Dumbbell"]` — list several to give the reader tabs |
| `tab` | which view the chart opens on: `"line"`, `"discrete-bar"`, `"map"`, `"table"`, ... |
| `hasMapTab`, `map` | the world map and its colour scale, region and tolerance |
| `ySlugs` | which columns to plot, space-separated |
| `xSlug`, `colorSlug`, `sizeSlug` | scatter plot dimensions |
| `selectedEntityNames`, `selectedEntityColors` | the selection and its colours |
| `minTime`, `maxTime` | time bounds; `"latest"` for the most recent year |
| `xAxis`, `yAxis` | `min`, `max`, `scaleType`, `canChangeScaleType`, `label` |
| `addCountryMode` | `"add-country"`, `"change-country"` or `"disabled"` |
| `hideRelativeToggle`, `hideTimeline`, `hideLegend` | which controls to show |
| `stackMode`, `sortBy`, `sortOrder`, `selectedFacetStrategy` | how series are arranged |

## columns: Grapher's column metadata

```python
Chart(df, columns={
    "emissions": {
        "name": "Annual CO₂ emissions",     # display name
        "unit": "billion tonnes",           # full unit, shown in tooltips
        "shortUnit": "Gt",                  # what axis ticks show
        "color": "#c8c8c8",                 # series colour
        "display": {"numDecimalPlaces": 1},
        "descriptionShort": "Emissions from fossil fuels and industry.",
        "descriptionKey": "Territorial emissions, excluding land use change.",
        "sourceName": "Global Carbon Budget (2024)",
        "sourceLink": "https://globalcarbonbudget.org",
        "timespan": "1750–2023",
        "origins": [{
            "producer": "Global Carbon Project",
            "title": "Global Carbon Budget",
            "citationFull": "Global Carbon Budget (2024).",
        }],
    },
})
```

Typed as `ColumnDef`. Unknown keys are passed through, so anything Grapher's
`OwidColumnDef` accepts works.

## Recipes

```python
# Line chart
Chart(df, config={"title": "Life expectancy"},
      columns={"life_expectancy": {"shortUnit": " years"}})

# Bar chart
Chart(df, config={"chartTypes": ["DiscreteBar"], "title": "Emissions in 2023"})

# Line + bar + map in one chart, opening on the map
Chart(df, config={
    "chartTypes": ["LineChart", "DiscreteBar"],
    "hasMapTab": True,
    "tab": "map",
    "map": {"colorScale": {"baseColorScheme": "YlGnBu",
                           "binningStrategy": "manual",
                           "customNumericValues": [60, 70, 80]}},
})

# Scatter plot with colour and size
Chart(df, config={
    "chartTypes": ["ScatterPlot"],
    "xSlug": "gdp_per_capita",
    "ySlugs": "life_expectancy",
    "colorSlug": "region",
    "sizeSlug": "population",
    "minTime": "latest",
    "xAxis": {"scaleType": "log"},
})

# Daily data: a column of dates needs no configuration
Chart(df_with_a_date_column, config={"title": "Weekly cases"})

# A confidence band is three series, with muted bounds
Chart(df, config={"ySlugs": "anomaly anomaly_lower anomaly_upper"},
      columns={"anomaly_lower": {"color": "#c8c8c8"},
               "anomaly_upper": {"color": "#c8c8c8"}})

# Interactive controls
Chart(df, config={
    "addCountryMode": "add-country",
    "hideRelativeToggle": False,
    "yAxis": {"canChangeScaleType": True},
})
```

## Fetching OWID data (owid.site module)

```python
from owid import site

data = site.get_chart_data(slug="life-expectancy")     # or url=...
config = site.get_chart_config(slug="life-expectancy")
```

`get_chart_data` returns a long-format frame (`year`/`date`, `entity`,
`variable`, `value`). For wide data, read the chart's CSV directly:

```python
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv(
    "https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/life-expectancy.csv"
    "?useColumnShortNames=true&csvType=full"
)
```

## Replicating a published OWID chart

Because `config` is Grapher's own format, a published chart can be replayed over
your own data. `local_config` keeps the keys that still apply and drops the
site-only ones (`id`, `slug`, `dimensions`, ...):

```python
import requests
from owid.grapher import Chart
from owid.grapher.notebook import local_config

published = requests.get(
    "https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/life-expectancy.config.json"
).json()

Chart(df, config=local_config(published, df))
```

`owid.grapher.notebook.translate_config(config, data)` returns that as Python
source, and `generate_notebook(config, path)` writes a whole notebook that
recreates the chart.

## Map colour schemes

"Reds", "Blues", "Greens", "Purples", "Oranges", "Greys", "BuGn", "BuPu",
"GnBu", "OrRd", "PuBu", "PuBuGn", "PuRd", "RdPu", "YlGn", "YlGnBu", "YlOrBr",
"YlOrRd", plus OWID's own ("owid-distinct", "OwidCategoricalA", ...).
